30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]

    33	/-- A finite-presentation model ring after extension to the final finite subextension. -/
    34	noncomputable abbrev Pic0FiniteStageFinalModelRing
    35	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k]
    36	    (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
    37	    (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat)
    38	    (relation : forall j, Fin (m j) -> MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
    39	    (M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k)
    40	    (N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k)
    41	    (j : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C) : Type u :=
    42	  N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M j
    43	
    44	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
    45	-- The comparison cancels two nested finite-subextension scalar towers.
    46	set_option maxHeartbeats 6400000 in
    47	/-- Scalar extension of a final finite-stage model ring recovers its exact atlas ring. -/
    48	noncomputable def pic0FiniteStageFinalBaseChangeEquiv
    49	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k]
    50	    (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
    51	    (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat)
    52	    (relation : forall j, Fin (m j) -> MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
    53	    (e : forall j,
    54	      k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
    55	        Pic0FiniteStageRing C j)
    56	    (M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k)
    57	    (N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k)
    58	    (j : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C) :
    59	    k ⊗[N.1] Pic0FiniteStageFinalModelRing C L n m relation M N j ≃ₐ[k]
    60	      Pic0FiniteStageRing C j :=
    61	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange M.1 N.1 k k
    62	    (Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M j)).trans
    63	      (pic0FiniteStageModelBaseChangeEquiv C L n m relation e M j)
    64	
    65	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
    66	-- Naturality elaborates the cancellation and model-comparison squares together.
    67	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    68	/-- The final component comparisons intertwine every scalar-extended finite-stage map
    69	with its exact restriction or transition map. -/
    70	theorem pic0FiniteStageFinalBaseChangeEquiv_naturality
    71	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k]
    72	    (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
    73	    (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat)
    74	    (relation : forall j, Fin (m j) -> MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
    75	    (e : forall j,
    76	      k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
    77	        Pic0FiniteStageRing C j)
    78	    (M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k)
    79	    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic M.1 k]
    80	    (mapM : forall q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C,
    81	      Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
    82	          (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q) →ₐ[M.1]
    83	        Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
    84	          (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
    85	    (hmapM : forall q,
    86	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
    87	          (AlgHom.id L.1
    88	            (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
    89	              (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
    90	              (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
    91	              (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))))).comp
    92	          ((mapM q).restrictScalars L.1) =
    93	        ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e q).restrictScalars
    94	          L.1).comp
    95	          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
    96	            (AlgHom.id L.1
    97	              (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
    98	                (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
    99	                (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
   100	                (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))))))
   101	    (N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k)
   102	    (q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C) :
   103	    (pic0FiniteStageFinalBaseChangeEquiv C L n m relation e M N
   104	        (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)).toAlgHom.comp
   105	        (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   106	          (R := N.1) (K := k)
   107	          (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   108	            (R := M.1) (K := N.1) (mapM q))) =
   109	      (pic0FiniteStageMap C q).comp
   110	        (pic0FiniteStageFinalBaseChangeEquiv C L n m relation e M N
   111	          (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)).toAlgHom := by
   112	  have hval : N.1.val = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom M.1 N.1 k := by
   113	    ext x
   114	    rfl
   115	  have htower :=
   116	    scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower_finSubext (K := k) N (mapM q)
   117	  rw [hval] at htower
   118	  have hcancel := AlgebraicJacobian.cancelBaseChange_naturality
   119	    (F := M.1) (L := N.1) (K := k)
   120	    (phiL := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   121	      (R := M.1) (K := N.1) (mapM q))
   122	    (phiK := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   123	      (R := M.1) (K := k) (mapM q))
   124	    htower
   125	  have hmodel := pic0FiniteStageModelBaseChangeEquiv_naturality
   126	    C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM q
   127	  let eTarget := (pic0FiniteStageModelBaseChangeEquiv C L n m relation e M
   128	    (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)).toAlgHom
   129	  let eSource := (pic0FiniteStageModelBaseChangeEquiv C L n m relation e M
   130	    (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)).toAlgHom
   131	  let cTarget := (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange M.1 N.1 k k
   132	    (Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
   133	      (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))).toAlgHom
   134	  let cSource := (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange M.1 N.1 k k
   135	    (Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
   136	      (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))).toAlgHom
   137	  let fN := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   138	    (R := N.1) (K := k)
   139	    (AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   140	      (R := M.1) (K := N.1) (mapM q))
   141	  let fK := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
   142	    (R := M.1) (K := k) (mapM q)
   143	  let g := pic0FiniteStageMap C q
   144	  change cTarget.comp fN = fK.comp cSource at hcancel
   145	  change eTarget.comp fK = g.comp eSource at hmodel
   146	  change (eTarget.comp cTarget).comp fN = g.comp (eSource.comp cSource)
   147	  calc
   148	    _ = eTarget.comp (cTarget.comp fN) := AlgHom.comp_assoc _ _ _
   149	    _ = eTarget.comp (fK.comp cSource) :=
   150	      congrArg (fun f => eTarget.comp f) hcancel
   151	    _ = (eTarget.comp fK).comp cSource := (AlgHom.comp_assoc _ _ _).symm
   152	    _ = (g.comp eSource).comp cSource :=
   153	      congrArg (fun f => f.comp cSource) hmodel
   154	    _ = g.comp (eSource.comp cSource) := AlgHom.comp_assoc _ _ _
   155	
   156	end
   157	
   158	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	# Naturality of affine scalar extension
    10	
    11	For an algebra map A -> B, base change carries Spec B -> Spec A to the
    12	contravariant Spec of the scalar-extended algebra map.  The tensor factors are
    13	ordered with the extension ring on the left, matching the finite-stage Picard
    14	ring comparisons.
    15	-/

    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct

    27

    29	
    30	variable (R K A B : Type u)
    31	variable [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    32	variable [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    33	
    34	/-- The affine base-change isomorphism with the extension ring as the left
    35	tensor factor. -/
    36	noncomputable def affineBaseChangeIso :
    37	    pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))
    38	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) ≅
    39	      Spec (.of (K ⊗[R] A)) :=
    40	  pullbackSymmetry _ _ ≪≫ pullbackSpecIso R K A
    41	
    42	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    43	theorem affineBaseChangeIso_inv_fst :
    44	    (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).inv ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
    45	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    46	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
    47	          A →ₐ[R] K ⊗[R] A).toRingHom) := by
    48	  simp [affineBaseChangeIso]
    49	
    50	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
    51	theorem affineBaseChangeIso_inv_snd :
    52	    (affineBaseChangeIso R K A).inv ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
    53	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    54	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
    55	          K →+* K ⊗[R] A)) := by
    56	  simp [affineBaseChangeIso]
    57

    11	# Finite tensor-stage descent of a pinned cocycle datum
    12	
    13	A `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `K ⊗[F] B` descends to a datum over
    14	`M ⊗[F] B` for a finite intermediate field `M/F`.  The datum is first descended to a
    15	finitely generated coefficient subalgebra, then that subalgebra is factored through one
    16	finite tensor stage.  The tower law for datum base change transports the certificate strictly.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory
    24	
    25	open scoped TensorProduct
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    31	/-- Spread a pinned cocycle datum over `K ⊗[F] B` to one finite tensor stage over `F`. -/
    32	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_finSubext_tensorStage
    33	    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
    34	    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B]
    35	    {C : Over (Spec (.of F))} {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 F} [IsAffineHom pi]
    36	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (K ⊗[F] B) pi) :
    37	    ∃ M : DatG0.FinSubext F K,
    38	      letI : Algebra F (M.1 ⊗[F] B) := Algebra.TensorProduct.instAlgebra
    39	      let ι : M.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B :=
    40	        Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)
    41	      letI : Algebra (M.1 ⊗[F] B) (K ⊗[F] B) := ι.toAlgebra
    42	      letI : IsScalarTower F (M.1 ⊗[F] B) (K ⊗[F] B) :=
    43	        @IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq F (M.1 ⊗[F] B) (K ⊗[F] B)
    44	          inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance
    45	          (fun x => (ι.commutes x).symm)
    46	      ∃ D_M : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (M.1 ⊗[F] B) pi,
    47	        D_M.baseChange (K ⊗[F] B) = D := by
    48	  obtain ⟨A₀, hA₀, D₀, hD₀⟩ := D.exists_fg_subalgebra_baseChange_eq

    51	  letI : Algebra F (M.1 ⊗[F] B) := Algebra.TensorProduct.instAlgebra
    52	  let ι : M.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B :=
    53	    Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)
    54	  letI : Algebra A₀ (M.1 ⊗[F] B) :=
    55	    f.toRingHom.toAlgebra' (by
    56	      intro c x
    57	      exact mul_comm (f.toRingHom c) x)
    58	  letI : IsScalarTower F A₀ (M.1 ⊗[F] B) :=
    59	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (f.commutes x).symm
    60	  letI : Algebra (M.1 ⊗[F] B) (K ⊗[F] B) :=
    61	    ι.toRingHom.toAlgebra' (by
    62	      intro c x
    63	      exact mul_comm (ι.toRingHom c) x)
    64	  letI : IsScalarTower F (M.1 ⊗[F] B) (K ⊗[F] B) :=
    65	    @IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq F (M.1 ⊗[F] B) (K ⊗[F] B)
    66	      inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance
    67	      (fun x => (ι.commutes x).symm)
    68	  letI : IsScalarTower A₀ (M.1 ⊗[F] B) (K ⊗[F] B) :=
    69	    @IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq A₀ (M.1 ⊗[F] B) (K ⊗[F] B)
    70	      inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance inferInstance
    71	      (fun a => by
    72	        change a.1 = ι (f a)
    73	        exact congrArg (fun g : A₀ →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B => g a) hfactor.symm)
    74	  refine ⟨M, ?_⟩

    77	    (D₀.baseChange_baseChange C (A₀ : Type u) (M.1 ⊗[F] B) (K ⊗[F] B)).trans hD₀⟩

     8	/-!
     9	# Conditional finite-Galois representability for Picard zero
    10	
    11	This is a conditional producer: it descends a finite-level representative only
    12	under the explicitly supplied orbit-in-an-affine-open instance.  It is not the
    13	arbitrary-field representability endpoint.
    14	-/
    15	
    16	set_option autoImplicit false
    17	
    18	universe u
    19	
    20	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    21	open AlgebraicGeometry
    22	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    27	
    28	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    29	
    30	/-- Conditional finite-Galois descent of a finite-level Picard-zero representative.
    31	
    32	The orbit-in-an-affine-open instance is the sole extra descent hypothesis here;
    33	this theorem does not claim arbitrary-field representability.
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableBy_finiteGaloisDescent
    36	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
    37	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    38	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    39	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    40	    {J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))}
    41	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange K L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J)
    42	    [((pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep).OrbitsInAffineOpen)] :
    43	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
    44	      (AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOver
    45	        (pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep)) where
    46	  homEquiv {T} :=
    47	    ((StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv
    48	      (pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep) T).trans
    49	      (pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver C rep T).symm).trans
    50	      (pic0GaloisInvariantEquiv (L := L) C T).symm
    51	  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f v := by
    52	    apply (pic0GaloisInvariantEquiv (L := L) C T).injective
    53	    apply (pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver C rep T).injective
    54	    simp only [Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    55	    rw [StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv_precomp]
    56	    rw [pic0GaloisInvariantEquiv_precomp]
    57	    rw [pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver_precomp]
    58	    simp only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]

     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0GaloisAction

     9	/-!
    10	# The quotient-side bridge for finite Galois descent of Picard zero
    11	
    12	A specified finite Galois quotient represents equivariant maps after base
    13	change.  This file records that statement in the over-category.  It is the
    14	scheme-theoretic half of descending a representative of `pic0TypeFunctor`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits
    22	open AlgebraicGeometry
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    25	
    26	/-- An equivariant map from the finite-Galois base change of an object over
    27	`Spec K` to a semilinearly acted `L`-scheme. -/
    28	structure GaloisEquivariantOver
    29	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    30	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    31	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    32	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) where
    33	  hom : pullback T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X
    34	  commutes : hom ≫ f =
    35	    pullback.snd T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
    36	  equivariant : (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L T.hom).IsEquivariant rho hom
    37	
    38	namespace GaloisEquivariantOver
    39	
    40	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    41	  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    42	  (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    43	
    44	/-- Pull an equivariant map back along a morphism over `Spec K`. -/
    45	noncomputable def precomp
    46	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
    47	    (h : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T) : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T' where
    48	  hom := pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w ≫ h.hom
    49	  commutes := by
    50	    rw [Category.assoc, h.commutes, pullbackBaseChange_snd]
    51	  equivariant := SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
    52	    T.hom T'.hom rho h.equivariant a.left a.w
    53	
    54	@[ext]
    55	theorem ext {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
    56	    {h h' : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T} (hh : h.hom = h'.hom) : h = h' := by
    57	  cases h
    58	  cases h'
    59	  cases hh
    60	  rfl
    61	
    62	end GaloisEquivariantOver
    63	
    64	namespace GaloisQuotientWitness
    65	
    66	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    67	  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    68	  {rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f}
    69	  {Y : Scheme.{u}} {g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)}
    70	
    71	/-- A finite-Galois quotient witness represents equivariant maps after base
    72	change, with no affineness assumption on the test object. -/
    73	noncomputable def overHomEquiv (w : GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y g)
    74	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) :
    75	    (T ⟶ Over.mk g) ≃ GaloisEquivariantOver rho T where
    76	  toFun a :=
    77	    { hom := pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom a.left a.w ≫ w.e.hom
    78	      commutes := by
    79	        rw [Category.assoc, w.over, pullbackBaseChange_snd]
    80	      equivariant := SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
    81	        g T.hom rho w.equivariant a.left a.w }
    82	  invFun h :=
    83	    Over.homMk
    84	      (w.universal T.left T.hom h.hom h.commutes h.equivariant).choose.1
    85	      (w.universal T.left T.hom h.hom h.commutes h.equivariant).choose.2
    86	  left_inv a := by
    87	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    88	    let h := pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom a.left a.w ≫ w.e.hom
    89	    let hw := w.universal T.left T.hom h
    90	      (by
    91	        dsimp [h]
    92	        rw [Category.assoc, w.over, pullbackBaseChange_snd])
    93	      (by
    94	        dsimp [h]
    95	        exact SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
    96	          g T.hom rho w.equivariant a.left a.w)
    97	    have ha : pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom a.left a.w ≫ w.e.hom = h := rfl
    98	    have heq : hw.choose = ⟨a.left, a.w⟩ :=
    99	      hw.unique hw.choose_spec.1 ha
   100	    exact congrArg Subtype.val heq
   101	  right_inv h := by
   102	    apply GaloisEquivariantOver.ext rho
   103	    exact (w.universal T.left T.hom h.hom h.commutes h.equivariant).choose_spec.1
   104	
   105	/-- The quotient universal-property equivalence commutes with precomposition
   106	in the category of schemes over `Spec K`. -/
   107	theorem overHomEquiv_precomp (w : GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y g)
   108	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
   109	    (b : T ⟶ Over.mk g) :
   110	    w.overHomEquiv T' (a ≫ b) =
   111	      GaloisEquivariantOver.precomp rho a (w.overHomEquiv T b) := by
   112	  apply GaloisEquivariantOver.ext rho
   113	  change pullbackBaseChange K L g T'.hom (a.left ≫ b.left) _ ≫ w.e.hom =
   114	    pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w ≫
   115	      (pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom b.left b.w ≫ w.e.hom)
   116	  rw [pullbackBaseChange_comp K L g T.hom T'.hom b.left b.w a.left a.w,
   117	    Category.assoc]
   118	
   119	end GaloisQuotientWitness
   120	
   121	namespace StableAffineOpen
   122	
   123	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   124	  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   125	  (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
   126	
   127	/-- Under the orbit-in-an-affine-open hypothesis, the glued invariant-ring
   128	quotient represents equivariant maps after finite Galois base change. -/
   129	noncomputable def gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv
   130	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] [rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen]
   131	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) :
   132	    (T ⟶ gluedQuotientOver rho) ≃ GaloisEquivariantOver rho T :=
   133	  (gluedGaloisQuotientWitness rho).toGaloisQuotientWitness.overHomEquiv T
   134	
   135	/-- The glued-quotient equivalence is natural under precomposition. -/
   136	theorem gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv_precomp
   137	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] [rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen]
   138	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
   139	    (b : T ⟶ gluedQuotientOver rho) :
   140	    gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv rho T' (a ≫ b) =
   141	      GaloisEquivariantOver.precomp rho a (gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv rho T b) :=
   142	  GaloisQuotientWitness.overHomEquiv_precomp
   143	    (gluedGaloisQuotientWitness rho).toGaloisQuotientWitness a b
   144	
   145	end StableAffineOpen
   146	
   147	end AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The finite-stage Picard glue as a scheme over its field of definition
    10	
    11	The finite-stage glue package already contains affine algebras over its final finite
    12	subextension `P.N.1`.  Their structure maps agree on overlaps, so they descend to the
    13	glued scheme.  This retains the finite-stage object over `Spec P.N.1`, which is the
    14	object-level input for the scalar-extension comparison with the separably closed atlas.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    22	open scoped TensorProduct
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    29	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    30	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    31	
    32	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    33	
    34	set_option linter.style.setOption false
    35	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    36	-- Projecting the dependent scalar towers from `P` requires a larger local synthesis budget.
    37	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    38	/-- The structure map from the finite-stage glued scheme to its field of definition. -/
    39	noncomputable def gluedMap
    40	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    41	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    42	    P.glueData.glued ⟶ Spec (.of P.N.1) := by
    43	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
    44	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
    45	  let A : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u := fun U =>
    46	    Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U
    47	  let B : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u :=
    48	    fun U V =>
    49	      Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V
    50	  let r : ∀ U V, A U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    51	    pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange
    52	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    53	  letI : ∀ U V, Algebra (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    54	    pic0FiniteStageAlgebraOfMap (r U V)
    55	  letI : ∀ U V, IsScalarTower P.N.1 (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    56	    pic0FiniteStageTowerOfMap (r U V)
    57	  let tau : ∀ U V, B V U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    58	    pic0FiniteStageTransitionBaseChange
    59	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    60	  fapply Multicoequalizer.desc
    61	  · intro U
    62	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U
    63	    exact Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U)))
    64	  · rintro ⟨U, V⟩
    65	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U V
    66	    change
    67	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A U) (B U V))) ≫
    68	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U))) =
    69	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau U V).toRingHom) ≫
    70	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A V) (B V U)))) ≫
    71	            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A V)))
    72	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    73	    rw [Category.assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    74	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    75	    congr 1
    76	    ext x
    77	    simp only [CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, CommRingCat.hom_comp,
    78	      ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom, RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,
    79	      AlgHom.toRingHom_eq_coe, Category.assoc, RingHom.coe_coe]
    80	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A U) (B U V)]
    81	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A V) (B V U)]
    82	    exact (tau U V).commutes x |>.symm
    83	
    84	/-- The finite-stage Picard glue, retained over the finite field `P.N.1`. -/
    85	noncomputable def gluedOver
    86	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    87	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) : Over (Spec (.of P.N.1)) :=
    88	  Over.mk P.gluedMap
    89	
    90	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    91	
    92	end
    93	
    94	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.

The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    Type (u + 1) where
  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
  EGA limit criterion. -/
  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom

namespace JacobianData

variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
@[implicit_reducible]
noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep

/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
  d.rep.homEquiv

/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g

/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep

/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm

end JacobianData

/-! ## η-defeq smoke tests (recon §5 lower-order unknown; `example`-level, nothing
registered)

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/

/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness
certificates, as the pinned Jacobian datum.  The representation is stated in the
`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that
`JacobianData.rep` is typed against. -/
noncomputable def JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    JacobianData C where
  J := J
  rep := rep
  locallyOfFiniteType := hlft
  quasiCompact := hqc

@[simp]
lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_rep (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).rep = rep :=
  rfl

/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/
@[simp]
lemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : T ⟶ J) :
    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).homEquiv g = rep.homEquiv g :=
  rfl

/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/

    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)

    (hcl : ∀ y : J.left,

    (quasiCompact_of_pic0_class_surjective rep lam hcl)

/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` over an arbitrary base field**: the identity component of the
scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor.

Unconditional — no `[HasRationalPoint C]`, and no `[HasPicScheme C]`. The two
inputs `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` requires are both available for
`PicSchemeEt C` without hypotheses on `C(k)`: the group structure
`groupSchemeStructureEt` (Yoneda transport of the étale sheaf's abelian-group
structure) and `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1),
extracted from the representability package).

This is the Jacobian candidate of the headline. When `genus C = 0` it is
`Spec k`, with no separate construction: the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is then
`0`-dimensional. -/
noncomputable def Pic0SchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicSchemeEt C)

namespace Pic0Et

/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is a group scheme** — PROVED, unconditionally.

The identity component of a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type is an open
and closed subgroup scheme (`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme`,
Kleiman §5 Lem. `lem:agps`(3)), and its group structure is the one transported
onto `PicSchemeEt C` from the étale Picard sheaf by
`groupSchemeStructureEt`. Neither step needs a rational point.

Stated as `Nonempty` because `GrpObj` is data and the identity-component
substrate delivers the subgroup-scheme structure existentially. -/
theorem grpObj {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    Nonempty (GrpObj (Pic0SchemeEt C)) :=
  GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism (PicSchemeEt C)

/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is geometrically irreducible** — PROVED, unconditionally.

`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible` (Kleiman §5
Lem. `lem:agps`): the identity component of a `k`-group scheme locally of finite
type is locally of finite type, quasi-compact and geometrically irreducible. Only
the third conjunct is taken here. -/
theorem geometricallyIrreducible {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    GeometricallyIrreducible (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
  (GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible
    (PicSchemeEt C)).2.2

/-- `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is locally of finite type over `k` — PROVED, unconditionally
(first conjunct of `isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`). -/
theorem locallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
  (GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible
    (PicSchemeEt C)).1

/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is smooth over `k`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, and a **true**
statement.

Kleiman §5: a group scheme locally of finite type over a field is smooth as soon
as it is geometrically reduced. Mathlib's `smooth_of_grpObj` takes exactly

over an arbitrary field, and the first two are proved above

characteristic zero, and a genuine characteristic-`p` statement otherwise. It
does not synthesize, and its only producer in the tree is
`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, which would be circular.

This is the étale-formulation counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.smooth`, and it is one

**assembly** rather than an obligation: the translation argument is mathlib's and
the two other inputs are proved above, so the obligation proper is
`geometricallyReduced` below and nothing else. -/
theorem smooth_of_geometricallyReduced {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-! # The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve

The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
its structure as an abelian variety.

## Status

The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
project from the witness directly.

The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.

`picardJacobianWitness` is wired to the `Pic⁰_{C/k}` development in its **étale** form
(`Picard/Pic0Et.lean`): the witness scheme is `Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C`, the identity
component of the scheme representing the *étale-sheafified* relative Picard functor. It
carries **no hypothesis on `C(k)`** — exactly the three challenge hypotheses and nothing
else — which is the owner decision of 2026-07-28 (protection I-0491) and the full strength
the challenge asks for.

Why sheafifying is what makes that possible. Over an arbitrary field one cannot ask for
representability of the *unsheafified* functor `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
(`picSharp`): Kleiman L5105–L5108 exhibits the conic `u² + v² + w² = 0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — a
smooth plane conic, hence smooth, proper and geometrically integral, over a field where it
has no rational point — for which he concludes `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable while
`Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is. The étale sheafification is Kleiman's own object; its sheaf property is
*proved* in `Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`picEt_isSheaf_forget`), not assumed.

**Two corrections to what this paragraph used to say** (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-30), both of
which had already been made at the seam and in the blueprint and were missed *here*, in the
file a reader opens first.

*The reason was wrong.* This said `picSharp` "is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally". No
source supports that for the **relative** functor: the lines it came from
(Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302) are about the **absolute** `Pic_X`, and `picSharp` is *defined* by
quotienting out `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. Kleiman's own claim about the
relative functor is the much weaker "not *a priori* a sheaf" (L1330), and `th:cmp` part 1
points the other way — `Pic_{X/S}` *injects* into `Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever
`O_S = f_*O_X` universally, automatic on these binders, so **in Kleiman** `picSharp` is
Zariski-*separated* here.

That last sentence is a statement about the SOURCE, and the Lean citation I first attached
to it does not carry it (`review-ajc`, corrected in the same session by a fresh-context
audit of my own fix). `PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`
(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) takes a `rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X`
hypothesis: it says a *representable* `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf, by subcanonicity —
which is the converse direction and is conditional on the thing the seam does not have.
`PicEtSubcanonical`'s own §4 docstring scopes it correctly as "only the first half"; that
caveat is what I dropped when I copied the citation here. Nothing in this project proves
`th:cmp` part 1. Do not restore a Zariski-sheaf reason in this slot; two replacement
citations have already been wrong in it (`I-0970`, `I-0973`), and this was a third.

*And "**false**" overstates what is proved.* The non-representability of `picSharp` is a
Lean theorem only *conditionally*:
`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) derives from `¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)` that no scheme
represents `picSharp C`. Its antecedent — that the comparison genuinely fails for that conic
— is **quoted from Kleiman, not formalised here**; doing so means exhibiting `φ^*O(1)` in
`picEt C (Spec ℝ)` outside the image via `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ`. So the accurate word for the
unsheafified statement over arbitrary `k` is **unproved with a refutation route mapped
out**, not "false". `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` says exactly this at
`fgaPicardRepresentability`, and says that writing "FALSE" here is the error the board row
was corrected for in the opposite direction.

## The five obligations, and none of them is false

Be precise about what the wiring buys, because "invoked upstream" is not "proved
upstream". The witness reaches **five** open obligations:

1. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` — representability of the étale-sheafified functor
   over an arbitrary field (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`). The project's central
   open obligation, expected to stay open;
2. `Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` — Cartier's theorem in characteristic zero, a
   genuine statement in characteristic `p`;
3. `Scheme.Pic0Et.universallyClosed` — Kleiman §5 Thm. `th:qpp&p`;
4. `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et`, 5. `isAlbanese_pic0Et` — the two leaves
   stated below, each at exactly the strength the assembly consumes.

Note (2) and (3) rather than smoothness and properness: `Pic0Et.smooth` and
`Pic0Et.proper` are **assemblies** over them, not obligations of their own, and citing
them as the open statements is a stale reading. What *is* proved unconditionally, and
measures axiom-clean: `Pic0Et.grpObj`, `Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible`,
`Pic0Et.locallyOfFiniteType`, `Pic0Et.isSeparated`.

**The five are NOT independent, and the list must not be read as five distances to be
added** — measured 2026-07-29 r2 (`ajc-p2`, `Picard/Pic0EtRelativeDimension.lean`;
independently reproduced by `ajc-p3`). Obligation 4 **implies** obligation 2: leaf B gives
bare smoothness by `SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth` and then geometric reducedness by
this project's `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, packaged as
`Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced_of_leafB`. So closing leaf B would close two of the
five at once, and obligation 2 is a *sub-problem* of obligation 4 rather than a peer of
it. What does **not** follow is that obligation 2 became cheaper: it is the weaker
statement, so proving it directly (the `k̄` reduction on `AJC.pic0av.structure`) remains
the right attack, and the implication is useless in that direction. The other three are
mutually independent as far as anything measured shows.

**All five are true statements awaiting proofs**, and that is the substance of the 2026-07-28
change rather than the count. The former leaf `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` asserted a
`k`-rational point from the challenge hypotheses alone; it was *false*, so the witness rested
on an inconsistent hypothesis and its consequences were vacuously true — a state no axiom
check can distinguish from an honest one. It has been deleted, never proved. The count was
five before and is five now; what changed is that no obligation is a false statement any
more.

That the headline carries no rational-point binder is **checked**, not asserted: the
`HeadlineBinders` section of `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` elaborates every headline

     8	/-!
     9	# Base change of the finite-stage Picard gluing
    10	
    11	The global base change of the finite-stage glued scheme is the scheme obtained by
    12	gluing its locally base-changed charts.  The chart and overlap pullbacks are identified
    13	with the corresponding exact separably closed affine opens.
    14	-/
    15	
    16	set_option autoImplicit false
    17	
    18	universe u
    19	
    20	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    21	open scoped TensorProduct
    22	
    23	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    24

    26	
    27	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

    29	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]

    31	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    32	
    33	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    34	-- Projecting the package retains nested finite-subextension scalar towers.
    35	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    36	/-- The base change of the finite-stage glue is the gluing of its base-changed charts. -/
    37	noncomputable def baseChangeGluingIso
    38	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    39	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    40	    pullback P.gluedMap
    41	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k))) ≅
    42	      (Scheme.Pullback.gluing P.glueData.openCover P.gluedMap
    43	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))).glued :=
    44	  limit.isoLimitCone
    45	    ⟨_, Scheme.Pullback.gluedIsLimit P.glueData.openCover P.gluedMap
    46	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))⟩
    47	
    48	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    49	-- The chart comparison elaborates the package's dependent scalar towers.
    50	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    51	/-- A chart in the base-changed gluing is its corresponding exact Picard chart. -/
    52	noncomputable def gluingChartIso
    53	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    54	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    55	    (U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :

    60	    chartBaseChangeIso C P U

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageAtlas
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.AbelianVariety.GroupSeparated
     8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Gluing
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# Affine intersections in the finite-stage Picard atlas
    12	
    13	The exact separably closed `Pic^0` representer is a group scheme over a field, hence is
    14	separated.  Consequently the intersection of any two affine charts in its chosen finite
    15	atlas is itself affine.  The canonical affine overlap packaged here is the geometric input
    16	for spreading out the finite atlas's restriction maps and gluing data.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    32	
    33	/-- The finite index type of charts in the chosen atlas of the exact separably closed
    34	`Pic^0` representer. -/
    35	abbrev Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex :=
    36	  { U // U ∈ (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).charts }
    37	
    38	instance : Finite (Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :=
    39	  (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).finite_charts.to_subtype
    40	
    41	/-- Pairwise intersections of charts in the chosen finite atlas of the exact separably
    42	closed `Pic^0` representer are affine.  This uses the group structure transported from
    43	the represented Picard functor, rather than adding separatedness as a hypothesis. -/
    44	theorem pic0FiniteStageAtlas_inter_isAffine
    45	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    46	    IsAffineOpen (U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1) := by
    47	  let J := (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1
    48	  letI : GrpObj J := (picRepDatumSepClosed C).grpObj
    49	  haveI : IsSeparated J.hom := isSeparated_of_grpObj J
    50	  haveI : Scheme.IsSeparated J.left := by
    51	    constructor
    52	    rw [← Limits.terminal.comp_from J.hom]
    53	    infer_instance
    54	  exact U.1.2.inf V.1.2
    55	
    56	/-- The intersection of two chosen finite-stage charts, regarded canonically as an affine
    57	open of the exact separably closed `Pic^0` representer. -/
    58	noncomputable def pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap
    59	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    60	    (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.affineOpens :=
    61	  ⟨U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1, pic0FiniteStageAtlas_inter_isAffine C U V⟩
    62	
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_open
    65	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    66	    (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1 = U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 :=
    67	  rfl
    68	
    69	/-- The canonical affine overlap is contained in its left chart. -/
    70	theorem pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_left
    71	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    72	    (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1 ≤ U.1.1 :=
    73	  inf_le_left
    74	
    75	/-- The canonical affine overlap is contained in its right chart. -/
    76	theorem pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_right
    77	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    78	    (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1 ≤ V.1.1 :=
    79	  inf_le_right
    80	
    81	/-! ## The canonical finite affine gluing datum -/
    82	
    83	/-- The chosen finite atlas as an actual open cover of the exact separably closed `Pic^0`
    84	representer. -/
    85	noncomputable def pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover :
    86	    (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.OpenCover :=
    87	  (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.openCoverOfIsOpenCover
    88	    (fun U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C => U.1.1) (by
    89	      apply TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover.mk
    90	      rw [iSup_subtype'']
    91	      exact (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).iSup_opens)
    92	
    93	/-- Every object of the chosen finite open cover is affine. -/
    94	instance pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover_isAffine (U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    95	    IsAffine ((pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).X U) := by
    96	  change IsAffine U.1.1.toScheme
    97	  exact U.1.2
    98	
    99	/-- The canonical finite affine gluing datum associated by Mathlib to the chosen open cover.
   100	Its transition maps and triple-overlap cocycle are construction output of `gluedCover`; this
   101	does not yet assert that the datum descends to a finite subextension. -/
   102	noncomputable def pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData : Scheme.GlueData :=
   103	  (pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).gluedCover
   104	
   105	/-- Every pairwise overlap scheme in the canonical finite gluing datum is affine. -/
   106	instance isAffine_pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData_V
   107	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
   108	    IsAffine ((pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).V (U, V)) := by
   109	  letI : IsAffine (U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1).toScheme :=
   110	    pic0FiniteStageAtlas_inter_isAffine C U V
   111	  let h := isPullback_opens_inf U.1.1 V.1.1
   112	  change IsAffine
   113	    (pullback ((pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).f U)
   114	      ((pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).f V))
   115	  change IsAffine (pullback U.1.1.ι V.1.1.ι)
   116	  exact IsAffine.of_isIso h.isoPullback.inv
   117	
   118	end
   119	
   120	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10

    33	
    34	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in

    36	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in

    41	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    42	    (U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    43	    P.glueData.ι U ≫ P.gluedMap =
    44	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    45	        (algebraMap P.N.1
    46	          (Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
    47	            C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U))) := by
    48	  unfold gluedMap
    49	  exact Multicoequalizer.π_desc _ _ _ _ _
    50	
    51	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    52	-- The composite infers the same nested tensor-product instances as the ring comparison.
    53	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    54	/-- Base change of a finite-stage affine chart recovers the corresponding chart in the
    55	exact separably closed Picard atlas. -/
    56	noncomputable def chartBaseChangeIso
    57	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    58	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    59	    (U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    60	    pullback
    61	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
    62	          (algebraMap P.N.1
    63	            (Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
    64	              C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U))))
    65	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k))) ≅
    66	      (pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).X U :=
    67	  pullbackSymmetry _ _ ≪≫
    68	    pullbackSpecIso P.N.1 k
    69	      (Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
    70	        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U) ≪≫
    71	    Scheme.Spec.mapIso
    72	      (pic0FiniteStageFinalBaseChangeEquiv
    73	        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e P.M P.N
    74	          (Sum.inl U)).symm.toRingEquiv.toCommRingCatIso.op ≪≫
    75	    U.1.2.isoSpec.symm
    76	
    77	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    78	
    79	end
    80	
    81	end AlgebraicGeometry

   171	    simpa [eTarget, eSource, f, g, pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange,
   172	      pic0FiniteStageMap, Pic0FiniteStageMapSource, Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget,
   173	      Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionSource, Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionTarget,
   174	      pic0FiniteStageRestriction] using

   176	        C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.e P.M P.mapM P.hmapM P.N
   177	          (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (U, V))))
   178	  have hinv : f.comp eSource.symm.toAlgHom = eTarget.symm.toAlgHom.comp g := by
   179	    ext x
   180	    apply eTarget.injective
   181	    have hx := DFunLike.congr_fun hnat (eSource.symm x)
   182	    simpa using hx
   183	  simp only [Functor.mapIso_hom, Iso.op_hom, Scheme.Spec_map,
   184	    Quiver.Hom.unop_op]
   185	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← Spec.map_comp]
   186	  congr 1
   187	  simpa only [← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp] using congrArg CommRingCat.ofHom hinv
